chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Heat on the road and caring for horns
summary: In Texas and Oklahoma heat the reeds cracked; they used wet towels, oiled pads, and later enjoyed the Selmer's built-in springs.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You ever find yourself in a situation where you ran out of reeds, or the reeds were no good and you had to either borrow some yourself or...?

Yeah. In Texas the weather was so hot and Oklahoma. It was like all0 at night -- in the daytime. Like when we get to the ballroom, it'll be like 100, you know, 90 and we play in shirt sleeves. It be (inaudible), you know. And Jeff and I, we used to put a glass of water down on the side. And when we get through playing a set, we wasn't going to (inaudible) play for a little while, we take off the mouthpiece and sit it in the water. Let it sit there. The horn would get so hot, the reed would just curl up and crack. (Inaudible) so hot out there (inaudible). The road was very rough on the reed -- and the horn too. What we used to do to keep our horn moist, we used to have big towels. We'd get great

big towels out of the hotels -- we'd take one, you know. And we'd dampen it, you know. And then we'd put it in our horn -- wet towel and put it down the bell of the horn. And then take the other towel and put it over -- you know, just lay it in there.

Yeah. So the heat wouldn't dry the horn out. You know, keep it moist. Keep the pads, because that time -- See, that time -- you remember when we was using those Conn horns, and the pad used to bust. (Inaudible). We had two or three sets. Then we used to oil the pads down with 3-in-1 oil to keep it from cracking. You know, the water (inaudible). You have to keep drying your horn out.
You had a lot of cork with you, I guess.
Yeah. But when we went into the Selmer, the

Selmer had the spring built into the metal, remember? Into the springs, they had a little thing sticking out there. The springs fit into that.
And we didn't have to worry about no cork and all that stuff. The felt -- Selmer had the felt.

It was glued on to -- You didn't have to have no more worry about horns on the road, or anything. When we went into the Selmer horns -- the saxophones -- we didn't have too much trouble. Very little bit of oil.
Keep your horn cleaned out and (inaudible) those pads would stay. Selmer pads were great.
